title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) to measure whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents with gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72; n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate contract this degenerate confirmatory outcome is expected when identical generated candidates produce no baseline execution faults. We report the preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, and artifact-grounded guidance for follow-on confirmatory designs able to detect verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are widely proposed to translate high-level operator intents into device-level network configurations. Intent→configuration automation can speed change pipelines but risks silently violating reachability, access-control, ordering, or workflow invariants and thereby causing outages if generated text is executed without additional checks. A common operational mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture that pairs stochastic LLM generation with deterministic verification (and optional repair or human review). Despite architectural proposals and prototypes, there are few preregistered, paired experiments that measure a verifier's detection performance against executed outcomes under tightly controlled semantics.

We address a narrowly scoped, preregistered research question: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? The paired estimand isolates detector utility from generator-side resampling, prompt engineering, or repair-driven improvements. We executed study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 across 72 preregistered paired intents (shared_initial_candidate semantics). The run completed without technical failures and produced a degenerate confirmatory outcome: no emulator-observed baseline faults (paired difference = 0.0). Rather than treating this as a failed experiment, we analyze why the degenerate result follows from preregistered design choices, document deterministic execution accounting, and give concrete preregisterable alternatives that enable non-degenerate inference when baseline error prevalence is non-negligible.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps research spans intent→configuration translation, tool-augmented orchestration, and GVR-style architectures. Prior empirical work shows modern LLMs can produce device-level configurations from high-level intent in constrained vendor-dialect settings and curated evaluation suites, demonstrating promising task-level accuracy but remaining limited in scope and dataset diversity [1]. Multi-agent and tool-augmented frameworks illustrate how verifiers and domain services can be integrated into agentic NetOps workflows to reduce regressions in prototype settings [2].

More generally, GVR patterns have been proposed and empirically studied in code and software-repair domains where deterministic validators improve downstream correctness when baseline generator errors are non-negligible [3]. Canonical network-verification techniques (header-space analysis and related analyzers) provide precise invariants for reachability and policy checks and are natural choices for the verify stage in NetOps GVR pipelines [4]. The supplied literature supports three core points: (i) LLMs can generate plausible device configs under constrained conditions [1]; (ii) system proposals show feasible verifier integration points [2]; and (iii) GVR can be empirically useful in other domains when baseline generator errors exist and repair/resampling is permitted [3]. What remains underexplored in the provided records is a preregistered, paired measurement that isolates verifier detection on identical candidates; our study targets that gap.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 before any execution. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The confirmatory hypothesis (H1) targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 (two-sided α=0.05, power ≥ 0.80); a sample heuristic gave ≈63 pairs and we preregistered N=72 pairs stratified equally across three difficulty strata. The full preregistration, exclusions, and sensitivity analyses were frozen prior to execution.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and experimental contract. The adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent we made exactly one initial LLM generation and evaluated that identical candidate in two paired conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record whether emulator-observed operational faults occur. Guarded: run the canonical deterministic verifier on the same candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no executed fault); if not flagged, execute the same candidate in the emulator and record the result. By construction, any paired difference can only arise from the verifier preventing execution of a candidate that would otherwise have failed in emulation; this cleanly isolates detector utility from generator-side resampling or repair.

Model, adapter, and verifier (artifact-grounded). The declared model is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json) requested via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; the verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 configured with the full_intent_constraint_validation rule set. Key recorded model configuration fields include declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", provider = "openai_responses", max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, and temperature = null. Recorded temperature = null indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics; this archived null value should not be interpreted as deterministic (temperature=0) sampling but rather as an explicit sampling-parameter uncertainty documented in the model configuration.

Task generation, contamination controls, and stratification. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest encodes a natural-language intent, an ordered required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, initial/expected_state snapshots, and a difficulty.level tag (medium/hard/very_hard). Exact-match contamination checks against a public-corpus fingerprint were preregistered; no confirmatory items were excluded. The confirmatory sample used 24 pairs per stratum as preregistered.

Execution, scoring, and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two retries for transient hosted-API errors. The run executed 72 shared-generation calls (one per pair) and 144 total episodes (baseline + guarded per pair). The verifier produces structured validator_traces per episode (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after snapshots, violation_codes, violation_count, difficulty metadata). The scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation enforces required_sequence order, allowed_touched_fields, and preserve_unspecified_state constraints from each task manifest. Per-episode scoring artifacts were archived to permit deterministic audit. All deterministic accounting, provider-call audits, and analysis scripts used in inferential steps are recorded in the execution and analysis manifests.
sections.results:
Execution summary and manifest. The autonomous pipeline completed without technical failures. Key manifest figures: planned_episode_count = 144; completed_episode_count = 144; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 72; artifact_count = 510. analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline successes = 72, baseline failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded successes = 72, guarded failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0).

Paired contingency and inferential outputs. Aggregating across 72 confirmatory pairs produced contingency counts n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (guarded × baseline). The paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) is [0.0, 0.0]. These values are deterministic consequences of the preregistered shared_initial_candidate contract combined with observed emulator outcomes: if the identical generated candidate never fails in baseline execution, the verifier cannot reduce executed faults under this design.

Representative validator diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show that parsed_command_count equaled required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for sampled tasks: for example, pair-000001 (medium) parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, violation_count = 0; pair-000002 (hard) parsed_command_count = 2, required_command_count = 2, violation_count = 0. These archived validator_traces indicate the verifier executed but produced no flags for the shared candidates.

Contamination and missingness diagnostics. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero exact-match contaminations for confirmatory pairs. analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 72 and zero failures or unscorable episodes. Pre-registered sensitivity analyses (treating excluded pairs as failures; bootstrap diagnostics) were executed; because no pairs were excluded and no discordant outcomes occurred these analyses reproduce the degenerate numeric conclusion.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the degenerate confirmatory outcome. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the estimand measures only whether a verifier can prevent execution of a candidate that would otherwise have caused an emulator-observed fault. In our run the identical generated candidates produced zero baseline emulator faults, so the paired difference is algebraically zero. This is an expected, artifact-grounded outcome rather than an inconsistent or inconclusive analysis result.

Attribution to aligned design choices. Archived artifacts allow concrete attribution of the ceiling result to measurable pipeline factors. (1) Task manifests encoded strict required_sequence and allowed_touched_fields, increasing the probability that a single correct generation satisfies intent constraints. (2) The declared model outputs frequently matched those manifest constraints (shared_initial_candidate traces). (3) The verifier enforced the same constraints (full_intent_constraint_validation), and its validator_traces show parsed_command_count = required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for representative tasks. The confluence of constrained intents, congruent verifier rules, and model outputs explains the absence of baseline execution faults.

Design and statistical implications for future confirmatory studies. A paired confirmatory test targeting a fixed absolute reduction requires a non-zero baseline prevalence of executed faults to have power. When baseline prevalence is zero, no paired detector effect can be observed. Practical preregistered alternatives that enable non-degenerate inference include: (A) independent-generation arms (allow separate initial generator calls per condition so the guarded workflow can influence candidate distributions via repair or resampling); (B) repair-enabled flows (permit verifier-triggered repair and execute repaired candidates to measure end-to-end improvement); (C) adversarial/fault-injection task banks (seed ambiguous or ordering-sensitive intents to raise baseline error prevalence); (D) sampling-parameter sweeps and multi-model comparisons (record explicit non-null temperatures and test multiple models); and (E) dedicated false-positive cost arms (quantify blocking costs by measuring flagged-but-safe candidates and downstream operator effort). Each alternative is preregisterable and compatible with the archived execution and analysis infrastructure.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates detector utility but precludes verifier-mediated resampling or repair effects; provider-call audit confirms one shared generation per pair. Construct validity: emulator-executed faults are a conservative surrogate for operational harm and do not capture traffic-dependent timing or hardware idiosyncrasies. External validity: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic task bank; extrapolation to other models, real-world task distributions, or production hardware is limited. Conclusion validity: with zero baseline faults the preregistered power analysis targeting a 0.20 absolute reduction is moot; future confirmatory designs must ensure baseline prevalence aligns with power targets.

Operational implication. The ceiling outcome does not imply verifiers are unnecessary. Rather, it documents a reproducible case where constrained intents, congruent verifier rules, and model outputs align such that execution faults do not occur. In operational settings with incomplete intents, noisy telemetry, or cross-vendor dialect mismatch, verifiers remain a principled guard. Measuring verifier net value requires explicit preregistered trade-off quantification (true-positive detection, false-positive blocking cost, repair effort) on task banks with non-negligible baseline faults.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to test whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under the shared_initial_candidate contract. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires preregistered contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons. The archived artifacts (responses, task manifests, validator traces, execution manifest, and analysis logs) provide a reproducible template and deterministic accounting for those follow-on confirmatory designs and power calculations.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock. Human role: a Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the immutable initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the lock. Models and orchestration: initial generation used gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json) via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") served as the canonical verifier; an isolated emulator executed candidate configurations. Preregistration: study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 was preregistered and frozen before observing outcomes. Immutable master-prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Artifacts and manifests (execution and analysis) were archived during the run to permit deterministic audit; the manuscript reports experimental design, execution accounting, and inferential outputs derived from those archived artifacts. No human manual manuscript editing or content insertion occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: the baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per-condition generation, multi-sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single-model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling-parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (sampling parameters unset); null indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics and should not be interpreted as deterministic sampling (temperature=0).

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact-match checks were applied, but private training-data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
